The Title IX process is usually not public, but records from the investigation were made public through Kretzschmar’s Article 78 proceeding, a lawsuit he initiated in state court after he exhausted his options at Cornell.
Lawyers for two of the accused men have denied wrongdoing, while the others have yet to release statements to NBC News. The Chi Phi chapter was barred from campus as a result of the allegations.

Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten defended his decision not to charge anyone this week, saying Jane Doe’s statement “described her participation in drug use and sexual conduct as voluntary, conscious, and consensual.”
Kretzschmar’s Article 78 proceeding, text messages and Jane Doe’s own statements show a more complicated reality.

Doe, then 20, alleges in a six-page statement to Cornell police that she arrived at Chi Phi after drinking heavily and initially entered an upstairs bedroom with two men she considered friends before things escalated. She told police she consumed ketamine for the first time that night and became increasingly impaired, drifting in and out of awareness as fraternity members filtered in and out of the room.

“You look like an operating human being. [...Y]ou don’t look dead or asleep necessarily. So lights are on, but nobody’s home. Your brain is not functioning at its proper level,” Doe said at a Title IX hearing in May, detailed in Kretzschmar’s court case.

Kretzschmar, however, described a far different scene when he briefly entered the room, saying in interviews with Title IX investigators that he saw nothing to suggest Jane Doe was incapacitated or in distress.

He “consistently stated in his interviews, documentary submissions, and at the hearing that he did not observe [Jane Doe] naked at any time nor partake in any drug use while in the alumni room” that night, according to the Title IX panel’s report.
For Subscribers

Admitting that he had seen the initial Snapchat message before he went in the room, he told investigators that he went in briefly because he was looking for a vape and did not know whether the message “was a joke or what was going on in the [alumni] room,” according to the report.

Cornell officials, in deciding to sanction Kretzschmar, noted in one filing that he“admitted he talked to someone about what was happening in the room and understood the person to say sexual activity was going on.”

Kretzschmar testified that he went into the room in part to “go down and check” because he heard from one of his brothers that the “free p----y” text was real and he wanted to see what was happening. He said he was also concerned about what may have been happening because of the odd announcement.
For Subscribers

Still, he replied in the chat around 2:30 a.m. Oct. 20, 2024, that his brother’s boast about a girl in the alumni room was “not a bit.” He told investigators at a May 2025 hearing that he was “following along with what everyone else was saying” and that it was “immature and dumb.”
“I shouldn’t have said it. And it is immature and a stupid text message for sure,” he said at the hearing, according to his court filings.

Doe, however, told campus police her experience was far more daunting. She told police she realized at some point that she had taken ketamine earlier and then did so again because she thought that “if I do Ketamine again maybe I will pass out. My thought was that if I passed out and these men had sex with me, then they could be charged with Rape.”

The next morning, after one of the defendants dropped her home and she slept for a few hours, she learned that her night had become campus gossip, according to the six-page statement she gave to campus police.

In the days after her assault, Jane Doe continued to text at least one of the men, initially expressing distress over the way the encounter was being discussed on campus, according to messages NBC News obtained separately.
The Chi Phi member responded with reassurances and a spin on the situation, including around Nov. 7, when Jane Doe began to doubt that he and his fraternity friends were not the source of the gossip.

“I understand the regret, but personally I don’t think you have anything to be ashamed of,” the Chi Phi member told her. “The only shameful thing is how this spread and how people won’t shut up about it-which just reflects poorly on them tbh.”
Jane Doe told the brother that she agreed “it’ll get better” and that “everyone needs to grow up cause sexuality and sex and s--t is changing and stuff like this is going to become more common.”

Jane Doe’s attorney previously told NBC News that his client’s messages with the accused men show that she was “traumatized after the assaults and was trying to process what had occurred and get information about what happened to her and who was involved.”

“She was numb and in shock at the time,” he added. “She was struggling to accept that somebody that she believed was her friend would violate and dehumanize her. It is common that survivors initially cannot accept what happened to them.”
The texts also seem to show Jane Doe’s demeanor shift as she realizes something was wrong. In one message, she tells the fraternity member: “yall aren’t my friends. yall are covering your asses.”

Days later, the fraternity member asks Jane Doe whether she had anything to do with his “being labeled as an assaulter in the public eye,” which she denies, saying, “i do know people are changing the narrative because like in any sexual scenario w one woman and many men the woman was probably victim” and “i know there are rumors i was gang banged.”
The next day, Nov. 8, Jane Doe reported her allegations to campus police, saying in a final message to the man: “i think i’m done talking to you. i know you lied.”

Kretzschmar’s own testimony in the Title IX investigation showed that, even as he denied having participated in the incident, he later questioned whether he should have recognized that something might be wrong.

“I was sorry that maybe if it wasn’t consensual and she was victimized, I was sorry for not stopping it,” Kretzschmar said at a Title IX hearing in May. “And that I’m sorry I couldn’t tell if she was under the influence…  just sorry that I felt like if something actually bad happened, I didn’t stop it.”

Ultimately, however, the Title IX investigative panel found that Kretzschmar understood that the Snapchat message he sent “indicated some kind of sexual situation involving a female” when he chose to enter the room and that the record supported its finding that he was responsible for attempted sexual exploitation.

The panel, however, did not find sufficient evidence that Kretzschmar took ketamine after it reviewed a November 2024 follicle drug test he provided independently. His punishments were focused on learning from the experience, according to documents filed in his subsequent lawsuit.

Kretzschmar had to write a reflection paper on “the specific circumstances for which he was found responsible,” along with “a detailed proposal for future University educational materials to train undergraduate students around the intersection of social media use and sexual harassment, as well as bystander intervention.”

He was ordered not to speak to Jane Doe for the duration of his time at Cornell and required to participate in a study at the Office of Civil Rights related to social media use, sexual harassment and bystander intervention. He was also required to help create educational programming for others about those issues.

Kretzschmar and his lawyers, however, argued in state court in Tompkins County that the process was fundamentally unfair, including because he was found responsible for an offense that was not listed in his initial set of administrative charges.
Among the arguments was that one of the panel members was in her car and driving during live testimony and distracted by other unrelated tasks throughout the testimony.

The judge who considered the challenge found it did not matter because the underlying theory was the same. In criminal court, state Supreme Court Justice Mark Masler wrote, lesser included charges are common.

“If a criminal defendant, whose liberty interests are at stake, maybe convicted of a lesser included offense with which he or she was not specifically indicted — including an attempt to commit the greater count — then the finding that petitioner was responsible for Attempted Sexual Exploitation cannot be considered to have been arbitrary and capricious,” Masler found.

If you or someone you know has been sexually assaulted, call the National Sexual Assault Hotline at 1-800-656-4673. The hotline, run by the Rape, Abuse, & Incest National Network (RAINN), can put you in contact with your local rape crisis center. You can also access RAINN’s online chat service at rainn.org/get-help.

title: Cornell survey showed increase in reports of nonconsensual sexual contact among female undergrads
summary: The findings are drawing renewed attention after the local district attorney said he was reopening a criminal investigation into allegations of a 2024 gang rape at the university.
story: More than 35% of female undergraduates surveyed at Cornell University reported experiencing nonconsensual sexual contact involving physical force, threats of force or incapacitation, according to a poll conducted last year, a figure that was up from 23% in 2023.
Overall, the survey found that 15% of all of the respondents reported such experiences, compared with about 11% in 2021 and 2023 surveys.

Cornell notes in its survey that a total of 6,000 students received email invitations to participate and only 926 responded, resulting in a 15% response rate, with 519 of those responding identifying as women. According to the report, the 2025 response rate was lower than in previous years.

The findings are drawing renewed attention after the Tompkins County District Attorney’s Office said it was reopening a criminal investigation into allegations of a gang rape at a Cornell fraternity house in 2024.
Eight universities that surveyed their students on nonconsensual sexual contact using the Higher Education Sexual Misconduct and Awareness Survey in 2024 showed rates lower than 30%.

In that survey, Washington University in St. Louis reported a result of 26.9% of respondents saying they had experienced nonconsensual sexual contact involving physical force or the inability to consent or stop the actions. Georgetown University reported 25.3% on the same issue in the same survey. Yale University and the University of Pennsylvania, which reported rates of 14.4% and 16.7%, also account for nonconsensual “penetration or sexual touching.”

Under state law, Cornell is required to conduct a campus sexual violence survey every two years. In 2017, the school developed the Survey of Sexual Assault and Related Misconduct and has administered it every two years since 2019.

In Cornell’s survey, alcohol was involved in many of the reported incidents, while the use of other recreational drugs was less common. Among the undergraduate female respondents, most reported that the incidents took place inside residence halls, fraternity chapter houses or annexes and off-campus houses.

Studies have shown that incidents of sexual violence frequently occur on college campuses during the first two months of the school year, a period referred to as the “red zone,” when students are going to parties and other events. According to the American Psychological Association, which cites a 2008 study, researchers have found that 50% of campus sexual assaults occur during the red zone and affect new students.

In a civil lawsuit filed earlier this month, an unidentified woman alleged that on Oct. 19, 2024, members of the Chi Phi fraternity sexually assaulted her for hours and she was pressured to take ketamine. The woman also said that one member had sent a message encouraging others to take part in the attack.
The fraternity chapter was barred from campus following the incident, but no one was criminally charged.

“While we cannot discuss the specific allegations during pending litigation, we take this matter seriously,” Chi Phi National fraternity said in a statement Sept. 18. “Our responsibility is to approach this with care for those affected and respect for a fair legal process.”

Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten said the woman’s lawsuit prompted him to reopen the criminal case. The case will be presented to a grand jury to determine if criminal indictments should be issued against the seven fraternity members named in the suit.
The suit said that some of the fraternity members involved were able to “mitigate their conduct” by writing essays to the university.

In a previous statement, Cornell said it launched a Title IX investigation that resulted in “a range of sanctions, which included expulsions and suspensions from Cornell. None of the individuals charged were offered the opportunity to write essays as a sole consequence of their involvement.”
“Any suggestion that the university did not impose consequential punishments for those involved is false,” the statement said.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

The lawsuit has sparked intense outrage over the handling of the initial sexual assault case in 2024. Van Houten defended his office’s decision not to seek criminal charges at the time, saying that the woman did not allege that she was raped or drugged against her will. According to Van Houten, the woman had described in a statement “her participation in drug use and sexual conduct as voluntary, conscious, and consensual.”
The woman’s attorney, Thomas P. Giuffra, has said that she was “traumatized” and “numb” in the days after the assault and was “unable to function or accept the horror of what happened.”
In a written statement, the woman said she wants “to recover from this trauma but it is extremely difficult.”
“It affects every aspect of my life,” she said in the statement. “It will haunt me and be part of me the rest of my life.”

The attorney for one of the men accused in the lawsuit of sexual assault, Scott Kretzschmar, denied he harmed the woman in any way, saying the lawsuit was “not only intentionally dishonest but morally repugnant.”

“He’s done nothing wrong other than being irresponsible and immature and inappropriate and ugly in those Snapchats,” the attorney, Jeremy Saland, said Wednesday. “But in terms of a crime, he was not involved in a crime, and nor was he aware of one because if he was, he would have reported.”

Another one of the fraternity brothers, Gillio Lopes, who is being accused in the lawsuit of sexual assault, also denied this allegation. “The public narrative now being advanced is incomplete and, in important respects, inconsistent with the record developed during the Cornell process, including many of Jane Doe’s own statements,” his attorney Andrew Miltenberg said.
Miltenberg said that during the initial investigation dozens of people were interviewed, there were multiple days of hearings and testimony, and an investigative report.

“It is these statements, contemporaneous communications, and other evidence that provide important context that is absent from the current public account. Those differences, and the evidence bearing on them, will severely compromise Jane Doe’s narrative,” he said in a statement.
The attorney for one of the other men did not respond to a request for comment. It’s not clear if the others have obtained counsel.

If you or someone you know has been sexually assaulted, call the National Sexual Assault Hotline at 1-800-656-4673. The hotline, run by the Rape, Abuse, & Incest National Network (RAINN), can put you in contact with your local rape crisis center. You can also access RAINN’s online chat service at rainn.org/get-help.

title: Federal commission approves construction plans for White House visitor screening center
summary: The center is part of President Donald Trump’s massive overhaul of the White House grounds but one that has garnered little to no opposition.
story: The National Capital Planning Commission voted unanimously Thursday to approve building plans for a new White House Visitor Screening Facility.

The project is part of President Donald Trump’s massive overhaul of the White House grounds, but one that has enjoyed bipartisan support and drawn little pushback compared to his other construction plans.

The facility will be built off 15th Street in Sherman Park, with an entrance that leads below ground for screening and allows visitors to exit by the East Wing of the White House, the site of the president’s more controversial ballroom project.
The commission’s chairman, Trump appointee Mark Paoletta, said Thursday, “I look forward to the beautiful building being built on the White House grounds.”

Lee Webb, an urban planner with the 12-member commission, presented the final plans for the facility. He said it will include a versatile indoor open-floor-plan space that will allow the Secret Service to install permanent screening technology. The space will also allow significant indoor queuing for large events, with a 700-person occupancy within the screening facility.
Visitors to the White House are now screened in temporary, double-wide trailers and tents, which the Secret Service has said fall short of its security needs.
The plans were approved by all members of the commission, which includes representatives appointed by Washington Mayor Muriel Bowser, a Democrat.
For Subscribers
Construction work is expected to begin in the next month and finish at some point in 2028.
For Subscribers

Representing the General Services Administration on the board, Trump appointee Paul Ingrassia hailed the addition of the new facility as “an incredible part of this White House reimagining we’ve been seeing.”
That includes the massive 90,000-square-foot ballroom that’s being constructed at the site of the former East Wing. The commission approved the plans for the ballroom in April.
At Thursday’s hearing, one of the presenters said the exit of the new facility will have Corinthian columns to “align with the ballroom’s language.”

The president has been highly involved in renovations at the White House, which have included gold adornments in the Oval Office and the installation of a helipad on the White House lawn, as well as other projects around Washington, like the proposed construction of a “Triumphal Arch.”

title: What undecided voters want to hear: From the Politics Desk
summary: Welcome to From the Politics Desk, a daily newsletter that brings you the NBC News Politics team’s latest reporting and analysis from the White House, Capitol Hill and the campaign trail.
story: Welcome to From the Politics Desk, a daily newsletter that brings you the NBC News Politics team’s latest reporting and analysis from the White House, Capitol Hill and the campaign trail.

In today’s edition, we chat with voters who remain undecided about key elections in their states in the final stretch of the campaign. Plus, Jonathan Allen digs into a striking admission from President Donald Trump.
— Adam Wollner
How undecided voters are weighing their 2026 election options
James Morton isn’t sure which party he’s going to support in November’s elections, and he doesn’t like his options.

Morton, a 67-year-old retired truck driver in Colorado, said Democrats have “gone too far to the left towards socialism,” while Republicans are “globalists” who “don’t care about the working-class people in this country.”

Morton, an independent who voted for President Donald Trump in 2024, is leaning toward backing third-party candidates in races for the House and the Senate this year. But he said his decision will come down to the high cost of living.

“The No. 1 thing is getting the cost of things back down, inflation under control, and pretty much that’s it,” Morton said. He noted that he and his wife have been buying different groceries as they navigate high prices.

Morton is among the 5% of voters surveyed last month in a national NBC News poll who said they weren’t sure which party they wanted to see controlling Congress after this year’s elections. NBC News spoke with 16 of those undecided voters as they weigh their votes this fall.

These voters feel little loyalty to either party — and many of them said that’s in part because they aren’t sure either party understands what’s important to them. Almost every one said high costs are top of mind.

In the NBC News poll, 50% of voters said they wanted Democrats to win control of Congress in the midterms, while 45% said they wanted Republicans to have control. How the undecided voters in between resolve their strong, sometimes conflicting feelings could ultimately decide what Congress looks like in 2027, from who controls the majority to how many seats that party holds.

Voters’ focus on making ends meet has been standing out in recent polling. In the latest NBC News survey, voters ranked cost of living and inflation as the most important issues facing the country, followed by government corruption and threats to democracy.

“I don’t like how expensive things are, and I don’t think anyone does,” said Aidan Valenzuela, a 19-year-old security worker in Texas who said he hasn’t decided whom to support in his state’s hotly contested races for governor and the Senate.
Read more →
Trump’s economic disconnect
President Donald Trump said yesterday that he’s done “a very bad job” of explaining to the American people why he thinks the economy is doing well.
For Subscribers
At one level, it was a rare acknowledgment from Trump — who has ranked himself as the greatest president in American history — that he has failed at anything.
For Subscribers
But there’s a disconnect between Trump’s view of the economy, which he and his advisers have been talking up since he reclaimed the Oval Office last year, and the sentiments of most Americans.

Interviews with voters across the country and public opinion surveys show that Americans disapprove of Trump’s handling of the economy broadly. Specifically, they are unhappy with his inability to curb inflation. Trump’s tariff agenda and the Iran war have put upward pressure on prices for everything from gas to groceries.
The disconnect threatens to further erode Trump’s credibility with voters who feel the squeeze of rising prices and interest rates but hear him describing the economy as strong.

With the midterms little more than a month away, it would be political malpractice for the president to tell voters that he’s failed on substance, even if he believed that. His challenge is to tell voters both that he hears what they’re saying about the economy and that it is better than they think it is — without blaming them.

For a while, Trump pointed his finger at White House aides, arguing that they weren’t doing a good enough job of selling his record. But his press secretary left, and there is no imminent plan to replace her.
Trump is, as he has always been, his own chief message-maker. It will be up to voters to decide whether the failure is in his delivery or in his policy.

title: Mike Tomlin gives fans a glimpse inside the Minecraft city he spent 12 years building
summary: For 12 years, the former Pittsburgh Steelers coach has been devoted to building a single map in the video game. On Wednesday, he showed it off for the first time.
story: As the coach of one of the NFL’s most successful franchises, the Pittsburgh Steelers, for nearly two decades, Mike Tomlin was charged with building championship-caliber teams.
In his free time, Tomlin was building something different: an elaborate cityscape in the video game “Minecraft.”

On his YouTube channel on Wednesday, Tomlin revealed part of that map, which he said he had been working on for more than 12 years. Within four hours, the episode had been viewed more than 334,000 times. By the next morning, that total had doubled.
“I’ve always had an interest in architecture and so forth,” Tomlin said in the video, which has amassed over 900,000 views. “And so I started building this creative city.”
Tomlin may have been perfecting the map for more than a decade, but his hobby had only become public three weeks earlier.

The 54-year-old stepped down as the Steelers’ coach in January after 19 consecutive winning seasons, which included a Super Bowl victory. As his debut season as a broadcaster for NBC’s “Sunday Night Football” began last month, Tomlin revealed in an interview with Craig Melvin that his passions, in fact, ranged beyond football.
Watching his then-young children spend hours playing “Minecraft” had inspired him to see what all the fuss was about. As they became teenagers and went off to college, their interest waned.
Not Tomlin’s, though.
“More than anything, it was therapeutic for me,” Tomlin said. “So, mindless entertainment. I’m not a big TV watcher. It allowed me to detach from the realities and the pressures of life.”

With the Steelers, Tomlin was known for unique sayings referred to as “Tomlinisms.” In 2020, he famously wouldn’t allow Covid restrictions to be used as a hardship, saying, “We do not care.” So it stunned some football fans last month to hear that what Tomlin privately did care so much for was a video game that is immensely popular with elementary-age kids.
Since its creation in 2009, “Minecraft” has become the bestselling game of all time, with more than 300 million copies sold, Microsoft said in 2024, and has since spawned a popular movie.

An open-world “sandbox” game, “Minecraft” allows users to build whatever their creativity desires using a variety of materials, from different types of stone and wood to beyond. Some players build fantasy worlds where building physics don’t apply.

Players often build in multiple maps. Tomlin stuck to just one, however, preferring to build what appears to be a midsize city centered on bodies of water and with a dense urban core that includes sports stadiums, high-rises and a PNC Bank. The map showed hills and wooded suburbs.
In other words, not all that dissimilar to … Pittsburgh.

Narrating his tour with a matter-of-fact delivery not out of place from his past weekly news conferences, Tomlin used verbiage a real estate developer would approve of while saying that his map all began by creating a bay. Then he built a boutique hotel, complete with an executive spa, therapy rooms and an “appropriate number of public restrooms.” Showing off a glass ceiling over the hotel’s conference room, Tomlin called his design philosophy “lighting-conscious.”
Mike Tomlin says he's been working on a city in 'Minecraft'

Some commenters online questioned how much time Tomlin had spent building while also working in the NFL, an industry known for its workaholic culture. Former Steelers running back Le’Veon Bell wrote, “we were tryna win super bowls and coach T was on minecraft building cities 😭.”
More so, the reaction tended to center on Tomlin’s dedication to realism.

“Never thought I’d watch Mike Tomlin discuss lighting and basement speakeasies,” one YouTube commenter said. On a Reddit thread devoted to Tomlin’s build, one person wrote, “When Mike Tomlin first mentioned this whole thing, I was NOT expecting such an impressive city!”

Tomlin built buildings by themes, intentionally placing them next to rivers, bays and lakes he carved out of the map. His designs are intricate; residential buildings included different floor plans for the penthouse than the lower floors. Kitchens featured islands. Bathrooms featured plants. Bedrooms included paintings. The living spaces in one high-rise, which was down the street from buildings named “CVS” and “7-Eleven,” wrapped around a central aquarium. Nearby were stadiums for professional soccer and baseball.

At some point, Tomlin acknowledged becoming “obsessed with rooftop penthouses” with great views. That focus then spilled over into designing spaces for indoor and outdoor entertainment, balconies, home offices and his-and-hers bathroom concepts.
“Find someone who loves you like Coach Tomlin loves a Jack & Jill bathroom,” another YouTube commenter said.

It was one of many jokes sparked by Tomlin’s “Minecraft” devotion. Yet, perhaps it shouldn’t have been all that surprising. In “Minecraft,” Tomlin seems to have found similarities to the mixture of creativity and discipline required in the world of the NFL. Coaches’ lives abide by a rigid structure of practices, games and the offseason calendar. They conceive exotic play designs and defensive coverages, then put them into practice by obsessing over details and precision.

“Football is an emotional game played by high-energy men who are really emotional,” Tomlin said in 2022. “They need to hear a steady voice. They need to hear consistency in messaging in belief, and so it’s my job to exemplify that.”

Tomlin was praised as a coach for his never-too-high, never-too-low personality. The kind of person whose idea of winding down after a long day in the spotlight might include ensuring his “Minecraft” map had a “certain density,” as he said. When Tomlin dropped his son Dino off at college, he said he was inspired to re-create the look of off-campus housing into his own city.
“Bro I used to come home sometimes and my PlayStation would just be gone,” one of Tomlin’s sons, Mason, posted on X. “And I wasn’t in trouble.”
At one point during Tomlin’s tour, he focused on a tall, beige building labeled “Trump Tower.”
“Not an endorsement,” a chyron said on the video. “This build is (circa) 2015… We didn’t think he would win. Twice.”
Its penthouse had an “unbelievable open floor plan,” Tomlin said approvingly.
He promised his roughly 76,000 YouTube subscribers more episodes.
“I’ll give you a tour of this aquarium at some point,” he said. “It’s crazy.”

title: U.S. pressures European allies to release diesel reserves as Trump considers export ban
summary: The Trump administration asked European allies to release diesel from their emergency stockpiles to increase global supplies and tamp down on soaring prices.
story: The Trump administration ramped up a pressure campaign Thursday to persuade European allies to release diesel from national emergency stockpiles. The White House says additional diesel from Europe would increase global supplies and potentially keep a lid on soaring prices.
The average U.S. price of diesel has soared by 70% since the war with Iran began, hitting $6.38 per gallon Thursday, according to AAA.
Less than five weeks before the U.S. midterm elections, Republicans are eager for any way to lower domestic fuel prices.

“Our European partners should accelerate delivery on their existing commitments and make additional supplies immediately available to address ongoing disruptions” to energy markets, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Thursday on X.  “American farmers, truckers, and businesses should not be left carrying the burden of a global diesel shortage.”
Shortly after Bessent’s post, Trump told reporters “we may” request that Europe release some of its emergency reserves.
Earlier this week, U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright had appeared confident that Europe would agree to tap its reserves.

“You will hear announcements from our friends in Europe about new diesel supplies that’ll come to the market that’ll meaningfully push diesel prices down,” Wright told reporters Wednesday at an event with Trump in the Oval Office.
But as of Thursday evening, those announcements hadn’t materialized.

U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said he raised the diesel issue at a G20 trade ministers meeting in Milwaukee this week. But he did not suggest that Washington had gotten any firm commitments about emergency reserves.
“We’d love to have a collaborative response” to the global diesel crunch, he told Bloomberg News on Thursday.
Also in Milwaukee were trade ministers from China, India, the United Kingdom and other countries that have been affected by strained global diesel supplies.
So far, however, the message coming from Europe on diesel reserves is a noncommittal one.
The E.U. is “in very close contact with our member states on this ongoing issue,” European Commission energy spokesperson Anna-Kaisa Itkonen told reporters at a media briefing in Brussels.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“We are also having high-level contacts ongoing with the U.S. administration,” she said.

The majority of Europe’s emergency diesel reserves are stored in Germany and France. Both American and European oil refineries have been running at near full capacity for months, churning out as much diesel fuel as possible.

While the Iran war is responsible for the lion’s share of price increases in crude oil and unleaded gasoline around the world, the price of diesel has been outpacing both of them since July, albeit for a different reason.
Russia has traditionally been a major exporter of diesel, but that stopped this summer after Ukrainian drone strikes destroyed Russian refineries.
On July 8, Russia banned the export of diesel in order to preserve its domestic supply. On Wednesday, the Kremlin extended that ban until the end of October.

“We’re tight on diesel because we’ve lost diesel exports from Russia,” Wright said at the White House. “We’ve lost diesel, some diesel exports from the Middle East, although we’re restoring those. And we’ve lost diesel exports from China.”
“That’s a lot of interruptions,” he said.

But whether Europe will tap its emergency reserves of diesel to increase global supply is complicated by the fact that the Trump administration is actively considering a move that is effectively the opposite of what it is asking Europe to do.
On Wednesday, the president mused about imposing a ban on exports of U.S. diesel.
“I’m thinking about it,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office. “I speak to Chris and Doug about it a lot,” he said, referring to Wright and Interior Secretary Doug Burgum.
“They sort of think ... it’ll help diesel, but it might raise the price of other things,” he said.
An export ban on U.S. diesel would hit European countries particularly hard.
It would also land at a moment when average U.S. prices for unleaded gas remain almost 50% higher than they were on Feb. 28, the day the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran.

title: Can red light therapy help your dog live longer? Here’s what vets say
summary: Red light therapy can help reduce joint pain and inflammation and help heal injuries. I asked vets about how to safely use a red light therapy device on your pet.
story: Red light therapy has many benefits: It can help clear acne, reduce wrinkles and even serve as a recovery tool post-workout by reducing muscle fatigue, joint pain and soreness. But what if you wanted to extend some of those benefits to your pet? After all, most pet owners will try anything to help their furry friends live longer and more comfortably.

When it comes to dogs, especially senior dogs, experts say red light therapy can be useful for relieving arthritis pain and inflammation. But how exactly does it work, and is it safe for all dogs? I spoke with veterinarians about the benefits of red light therapy for dogs and how to use a device on your pet. I also rounded up the best products to consider based on my experts’ guidance, as well as options NBC Selected editors tested on their own dogs.

Is red light therapy safe for dogs?

Red light therapy is generally safe for dogs, but using it incorrectly can lead to side effects. “The biggest practical risks with higher-powered devices are eye injury and thermal burns,” says Dr. Kate Elden, veterinarian and chief medical officer at Dutch, a pet telehealth company. “Across all the recent trials for arthritis, ear infections and skin issues, we almost never see adverse events reported.”

While red light therapy is usually low-risk when used correctly, that doesn’t mean it’s right for every dog. You should always talk to your veterinarian first, especially if your dog has active tumors (red light can stimulate cell growth and may speed up the growth of cancer cells, says Elden), active bleeding (can prevent clotting, which increases blood loss), reduced skin sensation (may cause nerve damage or injuries if they can’t feel the device getting too warm) or is pregnant (due to lack of safety data), says Dr. Lindsay Kendrick, the medical director at VEG ER for Pets in Boston.
Best red light therapy devices for dogs

If you got the green light to try red light therapy on your fur baby, consider one of the devices below. (Note: consult with your vet about whether it’s a good fit before you purchase.) This vest has two rechargeable pads that cover your dog’s back, chest and stomach. It’s also fully adjustable (it has a harness-style design with adjustable buckle straps) and cordless, so you won’t have to worry about your pet getting overly uncomfortable. It has both red light and near-infrared light, which helps reach your pet’s skin and joints and deeper into the tissue. You can change the intensity of the light using a button on each pad, and the vest has a 20-minute timer that automatically turns it off when the time is up. It comes in a medium and large size.

I tried this vest on my 8-year-old, 16-pound Havanese and bichon frise mix Bella, and I was surprised at how easy it was to set up and put on her. Bella hates having anything on her, whether that’s her harness, a sweater or boots. Since the vest is adjustable, it was so easy to find the right fit for Bella (who is mostly fluff), and she actually left it on for the full 20 minutes without much hassle. The Celluma Pro is a large panel that can cover your pet’s pain points and provide relief and reduced inflammation, specifically for larger areas (and bigger dogs), according to the brand. The panel is flexible, so you can turn it into whatever shape works for your pet. For example, if your dog has hip pain, you can fold it into an arch-like shape to cover both hips and legs.

“I’ve never used a red light panel like this one before, so I was a bit intimidated by it and didn’t know what to expect,” says NBC Selected reporter Zoe Malin, who tested the device with her 1-year-old mutt, Mabel. If you’re looking for an alternative to red light therapy, or simply hoping for another therapy tool to use in conjunction with a red light device, consider this pet bed from HigherDose, one of our favorite wellness brands. It has PEMF (Pulsed Electromagnetic Field), which uses gentle, low-frequency waves and low-intensity pulses to help improve circulation, reduce inflammation and support cellular health, according to the brand. Research shows that using PEMF sessions daily helps reduce stiffness and discomfort in dogs, and similar to red light therapy, it helps heal post-surgical wounds, fractures and soft-tissue injuries.

HigherDose already has a PEMF mat for humans, and just recently extended its line with a pet bed. I received the bed from the brand to try out, and Bella immediately loved it (which is surprising considering she already has three beds in our house). It comes with a remote that I use to adjust both the PEMF frequency levels (there are six levels that range from 3 to 60 Hertz) and infrared heat (which helps with stiff joints and is Bella’s favorite part). Plus, it has a machine-washable cover and comfy bolsters for her to rest her head on. It comes in two sizes: small (for cats and small dogs up to 25 pounds) and large (for medium and large dogs up to 75 pounds).
How I picked the best red light therapy devices for dogs

Most veterinarians I spoke to actually discourage selecting a red light therapy device on your own. “If home treatment makes sense, your veterinarian or rehabilitation specialist should recommend the device and provide clear instructions for using it safely,” says Elden. However, you can still use an at-home device if you first consult with your veterinarian and keep the following factors in mind:

Wavelength: “Wavelength and power are everything. If it doesn’t list these, don’t buy it,” says Elden. Look for wavelengths between 600–700 nanometers for skin/wounds, and 780–950 nanometers for deeper tissues like joints, says Elden. Red light versus near-infrared (NIR) light: There are two types of lights to look for in a device, depending on the kind of treatment you want to provide. “Red light is generally used for tissues closer to the skin, while near-infrared light may reach somewhat deeper,” says Kendrick.Red light also appears bright red, while near-infrared light is invisible to the naked eye. Keep in mind “there is no single correct strength, distance or session length for every dog, so a veterinarian should provide a specific plan for an individual,” says Kendrick.Clear instructions: The device should tell you exactly how to safely use it, including a timer and appropriate eye-safety guidance (more on eye safety below). “Ideally the manufacturer has published data using that device or at least provides enough technical information so that you know what you’re actually delivering,” says Elden. As always, consult with your veterinarian about how to properly use the device beforehand.FDA-cleared: Look for devices that are labeled FDA-cleared, which means the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) compares the device to similar, already cleared medical devices on the market and considers it “substantially equivalent,” according to experts in our guide to red light therapy.

Wavelength: “Wavelength and power are everything. If it doesn’t list these, don’t buy it,” says Elden. Look for wavelengths between 600–700 nanometers for skin/wounds, and 780–950 nanometers for deeper tissues like joints, says Elden.

Red light versus near-infrared (NIR) light: There are two types of lights to look for in a device, depending on the kind of treatment you want to provide. “Red light is generally used for tissues closer to the skin, while near-infrared light may reach somewhat deeper,” says Kendrick.

Red light also appears bright red, while near-infrared light is invisible to the naked eye. Keep in mind “there is no single correct strength, distance or session length for every dog, so a veterinarian should provide a specific plan for an individual,” says Kendrick.

Clear instructions: The device should tell you exactly how to safely use it, including a timer and appropriate eye-safety guidance (more on eye safety below). “Ideally the manufacturer has published data using that device or at least provides enough technical information so that you know what you’re actually delivering,” says Elden. As always, consult with your veterinarian about how to properly use the device beforehand.

FDA-cleared: Look for devices that are labeled FDA-cleared, which means the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) compares the device to similar, already cleared medical devices on the market and considers it “substantially equivalent,” according to experts in our guide to red light therapy.
Can red light therapy help your dog live longer?

Red light therapy, usually called photobiomodulation therapy or PBMT, uses red or near-infrared light to affect how cells produce energy and communicate. Though it can’t guarantee a longer life, red light and near-infrared light may help cells function better and calm inflammation, which can help reduce pain and benefit the healing process, says Elden.

“The strongest evidence we have right now is for musculoskeletal issues, specifically osteoarthritis,” says Elden. “We see dogs getting better range of motion in joints, moving around more and having less pain. It’s also showing promising results for wound healing, surgical incisions and certain skin infections.”

However, the research is growing but still mixed. There are some solid, randomized controlled trials showing clear benefits for osteoarthritis and post-op pain. But a 2023 systematic review found that a lot of older studies had poor designs, small sample sizes or didn’t report their laser settings properly, which makes the results hard to trust, says Elden. The well-established benefits are limited to joint pain and wound healing, especially when used alongside other treatments like exercise and weight management.
Frequently asked questions

Though studies are limited, the vast majority that do exist show there may be benefit of PBMT as an adjunct therapy to other treatments and tools. “It may help with infection control for infected dermatologic wounds and it may help with pain control for osteoarthritis, and it may lead to decreased need for usage of more traditional therapy such as antibiotics and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory conditions,” says Dr. Stephanie Liff, owner and medical director of Pure Paws Veterinary Care in New York City.

“We use it to make our primary medical treatments work better,” says Elden. Red light therapy can support (but not replace) exercise, medication and regular veterinary care. “It fits perfectly as a tool to improve mobility and comfort. “For an older arthritic dog, you want them exercising to maintain muscle, but it hurts. Red light therapy drops the pain and inflammation so they can handle their physical therapy, which helps with weight management, which further helps the joints. It’s part of a multimodal plan,” says Elden.
Never aim the light at your pet’s eyes, and make sure to have special protective eyewear for your dog and everyone nearby, says Kendrick.

You’ll sometimes see red light therapy devices marketed specifically for pets, but the basic technology is similar to ones you may use at home. “The light itself doesn’t know whether it’s treating a dog or a human. But human devices aren’t built for patients covered in fur,” says Elden. “Fur blocks light penetration, and darker coats can block even more. So, veterinary lasers often have different heads to part the hair or use specific wavelengths to push through it.”

Research even suggests that your dog’s coat color and whether the area is shaved can significantly change how much light reaches the tissue. So, if you use a human device, you usually have to clip the dog’s fur for it to work, says Elden.

However, even a device marketed for pets needs to be used with caution: “A ‘for pets’ label does not guarantee that a device is safe or effective, and a human device should not be used on a dog without veterinary guidance,” says Kendrick.
Yes, in rare cases you could see thermal injury to treated tissue and if you did treat near the eyes, you could see ocular damage including damage to their vision, says Liff.
Meet our veterinarians

At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also take steps to ensure all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and without undisclosed financial conflicts of interest.

title: Pope Leo Sent White Sox A Letter of ‘Abundant Blessings.’ Then They Won Their Playoff Series
summary: Considering how their Wild Card series ended, it appears that the Chicago White Sox truly are #blessed.
story: Considering how their Wild Card series ended, it appears that the Chicago White Sox truly are #blessed.

The team clinched their playoff series Sept. 30 against the Houston Astros after a two-game sweep at Daikin Park in Texas. But as many fans have joked, the historic victory — their first postseason series win in more than two decades — may have been in part due to a bit of divine intervention. It turns out that well-known White Sox fan Pope Leo XIV sent the team a special letter ahead of the high-stakes games.

“I willingly invoke the Almighty’s abundant blessings upon you and your loved ones,” the Pope wrote in the signed letter to White Sox chairman Jerry Reinsdorf that arrived Sept. 29, according to the team’s social media accounts.

The American League Wild Card series win marks the White Sox’ first postseason series victory since they won the World Series in 2005. That championship was coincidentally also against the Astros. And oddly enough, Pope Leo was in the stands for the series opener, rooting his Sox on from Section 140, Row 19, Seat 2.

This time around, the White Sox beat their Texas opponents in just two games for the best-of-three series. The mail that arrived from the Pope, which was dated Sept. 9, referenced a letter that he wrote ahead of the Winter Olympic Games in February.

“As I have noted, ‘sport can truly become a school of life, where all can learn that abundance does not come from victory at any cost, but from sharing, from respecting others and from the joy of walking together,’” he wrote, citing the February letter.

The pope added that it is his “hope that the White Sox will continue to foster bonds of friendship and solidarity among people, and thus bear hopeful witness to the possibility of living and working together in peace.”
Pope Leo’s love of the White Sox is well-documented. In June 2025, he repped his team, stepping out in a Sox cap while meeting newlywed couples at the Vatican.

The South Side team has been more than happy to embrace their famous fan. Earlier in the season, the team gave away White Sox-themed papal miters to fans who attended the team’s Aug. 11 game against the Cincinnati Reds. Weeks later, South Side native Father Tom McCarthy presented the pope with one of the hats as well.
The Chicago White Sox will move on to the American League Division Series, where they will take on the Cleveland Guardians starting Oct. 3.

title: Alix Earle Says the Last Book She Read Was Dr. Seuss. Jenna Has a Reading Syllabus for Her
summary: Alix Earle says she has never read a book, so Jenna Bush Hager is here to help.
story: Alix Earle says she has never read a book, so Jenna Bush Hager is here to help.

The creator of the Read with Jenna book club broke out a reading list for the social media star on TODAY Oct. 1 after Earle, 25, told Interview magazine that she’s “never read a book,” except for “maybe Dr. Seuss.” The revelation sparked backlash and shocked Jenna.
“Alix, you’ve been on the show,” Jenna said on TODAY. “We know that you’re smart, so you know what we want to do, we want to give you a little syllabus.”
Earle reacted to her comment going viral on her Instagram story by reposting a tweet about it, adding the caption, “This is sending me,” per EW.
Before Jenna broke out her reading recommendations for Earle, she and Sheinelle talked about the benefits of curling up wth a book.

“With social media, you have to use your mind quickly,” Jenna said. “When you sit in a book and you’re there for a while it uses a different part of our brain, which is a part that we used a lot back in the day and has been sort of combated with the rise of short videos.
“Reading fiction brings about — and we know this — the rise of empathy,” she continued. “Because you’re sitting in the shoes of somebody else.”
With that said, she offered the following books for Earle.
“Come here, sit on our show, and we can teach you how to be a great reader,” Jenna said.
‘The Baby-Sitter’s Club’
Jenna first recommended the classic children’s book series by Ann M. Martin.
“We know you’re an entrepreneur,” Jenna said. “She started her own brand. This talks about females getting together, starting a club, empowering each other. Let’s start here, Alix.”
‘Are You There God? It’s Me, Margaret’
Judy Blume’s iconic 1970 novel about sixth-grader Margaret Simon has been a rite-of-passage read for generations of kids.
“Alix, if you haven’t learned about sex, this might hit the ticket,” Jenna joked.
‘Of Mice and Men’
The 1937 novella by John Steinbeck about the Depression-era experiences of George Milton and Lennie Small is a staple of scholastic reading lists.
“If you didn’t get assigned this in eighth grade, I want to talk to your English teacher,” Jenna said.
‘Pachinko’
A more contemporary classic, the 2017 novel by Min Jin Lee follows the saga of multiple generations of a Korean family who move to Japan.
“I love this author so much,” Jenna said before showing off the weighty tome. “This is a bigger one, so that’s why you start with these (other books).”
Jenna wasn’t done, and she included a syllabus with seven more books:

title: Leigh Bardugo Reflects on Backlash to ‘Ninth House,’ Her First Novel Written For Adults
summary: Leigh Bardugo looked back at the uproar over content warnings in Ninth House and whether she thinks trigger warnings are necessary.
story: Leigh Bardugo is looking back at a conversation-starting chapter of her career.

The author rose to fame with her sprawling Grishaverse YA novels, set in a magical world. In 2019, she made her adult debut with “Ninth House,” the first book in a trilogy that unfolds among the secret societies of Yale.

At the time of its publication, a graphic assault scene in “Ninth House” sparked a discussion about content warnings. Some readers said they were shocked and disturbed by the scene and that there should have been a warning before reading.
On an episode of Jenna Bush Hager’s “Open Book with Jenna” out Oct. 1, Bardugo said the uproar is “still surprising” to her, “given some of the things that are popular now.”
“There was nothing in this book that really deviated from what you would find in any horror novel or urban fantasy novel, but it was a departure from what I had written for teens,” she said.
Bardugo said while there’s “an argument to be made” for content warnings, she noted that calls for them tend to be loudest for books written by women who previously wrote books for kids.
“I think there’s a very puritanical streak that runs through all this,” she said.
She also said if content warnings are expected, they need to be in every book, “and I’m not interested in being the test case.”

“I believe that things belong on different shelves,” she said. “That where we shelve a book is all about expectations. And if you are coming to a young adult shelf, you would never find ‘Ninth House’ there.”
Bardugo said her first impulse was to be defensive over the backlash to her book’s content. “I didn’t write this for shock value,” she remembered thinking.
Then, she realized the outrage was proof the book was working.

“You should be troubled by this. If you’re reading about an assault on the page. You shouldn’t just be able to skim right past it. It should hit you. It should hit you like a ton of bricks. And if I did that, maybe I did something right,” she said.
Ultimately, she said, the book “found the people it needed to find.” If she had changed or softened its contents, “it would not have found those people.”
Plus, she said, books are an excellent place to raise difficult and uncomfortable topics, “because you’re safe when you’re doing it.”

“(Books) can lead to conversation. They can lead to difficult thoughts that we have about things we’ve been through, things that we’re going through with other people, things that our friends have been through, that maybe we don’t know how to speak to them about. That kind of connection exists in these places of discomfort,” she says.
The final installment of Bardugo’s “Ninth House” series, called “Dead Beat,” came out Sept. 15, wrapping up Alex Stern’s voyage through the magical portals of Yale University.
